title: KPI Development & Performance Metrics
metaDescription: Building the Track, Trend, Measure, Improve model in practice, with automated KPI capture, leading and lagging indicators, and Best-in-Class benchmarking.
heroDek: A performance indicator that only shows up after the event is a record, not a metric. GSS builds the instrumentation that separates leading indicators from lagging ones, so decline is visible while there is still time to act on it.
contextHeading: Measure performance before problems become events
contextParagraphs: Most organizations already collect performance data. The challenge is turning that data into information leadership can use. Important measures are often spread across different systems, and indicators of what has already happened can overshadow the trends that show where performance may be starting to decline.

GSS develops KPI programs that bring those measures together and distinguish between leading and lagging indicators. Performance is tracked over time and measured against defined Best-in-Class standards rather than relying only on an organization's past performance, allowing emerging issues to be identified earlier. Where possible, data collection is automated using existing systems, reducing the administrative work required to maintain the program and giving leadership a consistent view of performance.

The goal is not simply to build a dashboard. The program must remain useful after the engagement ends. GSS establishes clear thresholds, reporting processes, and improvement priorities so organizations can identify negative trends, understand where attention is needed, and take action before those trends become larger problems.

methodology.label: Indicator Selection
methodology.body: Leading and lagging indicators are selected and defined against the organization's specific mission and existing data sources, not copied from a generic KPI library.

methodology.label: Best-in-Class Benchmarking
methodology.body: Target thresholds are set against defined Best-in-Class criteria, drawn from industry-standard principles, rather than the organization's own historical baseline.

methodology.label: Automated Capture
methodology.body: Data pulls are built from existing systems of record wherever possible, so ongoing collection doesn't depend on a manual roll-up.

methodology.label: Trend Separation
methodology.body: Leading and lagging indicators are trended separately, so a decline in the leading set is visible before it produces a lagging-indicator event.

methodology.label: Threshold & Escalation Design
methodology.body: Thresholds are set with defined escalation paths, so a breach reaches the right leadership level automatically instead of waiting for a quarterly review.

methodology.label: Roadmap Integration
methodology.body: Persistent gaps against Best-in-Class criteria feed directly into the improvement roadmap rather than sitting as an unresolved dashboard color.

coreCapabilities: Automated KPI capture from systems of record

faq.a: Not necessarily. GSS builds capture against the systems an organization already runs wherever feasible; new tooling is recommended only where the existing systems genuinely can't support automated capture.

faq.q: What counts as a leading indicator in a security program?
faq.a: Examples include training currency, overdue corrective actions, equipment out-of-service time, and self-assessment finding trends. These are indicators that move before an actual security or safety event does, not after.

faq.q: Who owns the KPI program once GSS leaves?
faq.a: Ownership transfers to site leadership before the engagement closes, with escalation paths and thresholds documented so the program runs without GSS in the loop day to day.
